description: Every number the child bodies are built from, with its source. tools/body/build.mjs reads this file and nothing else for them; facts and measurements are not copyrightable, and no drawing was traced. A `model` entry is our own modelling choice, said as such.
ageReason: One reference age for both children: 8 years sits in the middle of the 6-10 range, before puberty (no sex difference in the organs modelled), with every growth plate open and the bladder still rising out of the pelvis; one body per schema value keeps the package small.

sources.cdc2000: Kuczmarski RJ, Ogden CL, Guo SS, et al. 2000 CDC Growth Charts for the United States: methods and development. Vital Health Stat 11. 2002;(246). Data file statage.csv (stature-for-age, 2 to 20 years), https://www.cdc.gov/growthcharts/data/zscore/statage.csv.
sources.makehuman: MakeHuman 1.x base mesh and macro targets (makehumancommunity/makehuman at a8bc2d54ff0ac92e78ff71431b1023eda42bf482, makehuman/data), CC0 1.0.
sources.dhingra2010: Dhingra B, Sharma S, Mishra D, Kumari R, Pandey RM, Aggarwal S. Normal values of liver and spleen size by ultrasonography in Indian children. Indian Pediatr. 2010;47:487-492. Table II.
sources.obrycki2022: Obrycki Ł, Sarnecki J, Lichosik M, et al. Kidney length normative values in children aged 0-19 years: a multicenter study. Pediatr Nephrol. 2022;37:1075-1085 (CC BY). Table 2.
sources.francis1985: Francis IR, Glazer GM, Bookstein FL, Gross BH. The thymus: reexamination of age-related changes in size and shape. AJR Am J Roentgenol. 1985;145:249-254.
sources.maresh1938: Maresh MM, Washburn AH. Size of the heart in healthy children. Am J Dis Child. 1938;56:33-60.
sources.hakenberg1983: Hakenberg OW, et al. J Urol. 1983;130:249-251: expected bladder capacity (mL) = (age in years + 2) × 30.
sources.moore: Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR. Clinically Oriented Anatomy. Pelvis: in infants and young children the urinary bladder lies in the abdomen even when empty; it begins to enter the greater pelvis at about 6 years and lies wholly in the pelvis only after puberty.
sources.ponseti1978: Ponseti IV. Growth and development of the acetabulum in the normal child. J Bone Joint Surg Am. 1978;60:575-585: the triradiate cartilage joins ilium, ischium and pubis until early adolescence.
sources.ogden1984: Ogden JA. Radiology of postnatal skeletal development. X. Patella and tibial tuberosity. Skeletal Radiol. 1984;11:246-257: the patella ossifies from centres appearing at 3-6 years; at 8 the ossified part is smaller than the cartilage model.
